beast_pools.trs: Your exhaustion has a rhythm, a quiet but relentless hum in the back of your brain. It tells you that you're beating against an unyielding wall with a stick, that there isn't a point in trying to find a lock that won't open. It whispers to you that you can, should, and will help the next person you meet determine what to do with themselves, that perhaps that's even better. There is no resistance against this inevitable descent, just a slow, steady, final fall.

beast_pools.trs: If you've read Schopenhauer, you know the will is blind and the world is huge, so stopping is actually a relief. No point continuing to exist when life feels like a dreadful mechanical ache; just leave while the pain gets worse.
